info.title: Cargo Controller Import API
info.description:
## Reading Guide Below is an explanation for implementing the Cargo Controller Import API. The first sections contain information about the configuration and authentication for the API and the Webhook. In the following sections, an explanation about the endpoints can be found. Those sections consist of: 1. An introduction (including testing possibilities) 2. Information (such as requirements and constraints) about the request 3. Information about the response. See 'Responses' and ‘Webhook events’ 4. Request and response samples. Please refer to the sections on the right of the screen. If you want to download **example messages**, please use the 'Copy' button in the 'Response samples' in the specific sections. Do you want more information about the **JSON schemas**? All information (including these schemas) can be downloaded at the top of this page. # About this API The Cargo Controller Import API is used for tracking cargo and receiving real-time updates on your tracked cargo. After tracking a Bill of Lading (see Track requests section), you will automatically receive all updates on it. All data for that updated Bill of Lading will be sent to a special webhook endpoint configured for your organisation. See for more information: * Changelog * Functional scenarios regarding Cargo Controller Import API * Functional scenarios regarding Secure Chain API Events that trigger the webhook are summarized in the Webhook events section. # Configuration The API configuration and implementation consists of the following steps: 1. Set up and configuration 2. Send request to Cargo Controller Import API
using properties 'Portbase-access-key-id' and 'Portbase-secret-access-key' in the authentication headers and processing the responses 3. Receive and process Webhook events
(Cargo Controller POST requests to your endpoint) and validate the JSON Web Token (JWT) using property 'x-portbase-webhook' from the authentication headers ## 1. Set up ### API access Authentication is managed by using special Portbase authentication headers named 'Portbase-access-key-id' and 'Portbase-secret-access-key'. Your access keys will be emailed to the administrator of your organisation (as nominated in your service application). If you are a software supplier, then it concerns your client’s organization. ### Webhook configuration All webhook configuration is managed by Portbase. Please contact our sales department (sales@portbase.com) if you would like to register a webhook. Along with a url, one or more email addresses are mandatory to which we can reach out if an error on your webhook occurred. It is possible to register multiple webhooks. ## 2. Send request to Cargo Controller Import API Information about implementing the Cargo Controller Import API endpoints can be found at Cargo Controller Import API section. You can use the Functional scenarios section to review the different message flows. ## 3. Receive and process Webhook events A so-called 'webhook' (also known as web callback or HTTP push API) allows you to efficiently build a custom integration with Cargo Controller. As soon as they occur, we will send updates concerning your tracked cargo to your preconfigured webhook. For each update on your tracked cargo, we will post an HTTP call to the URL that you specify in your configuration. Therefore, your endpoint must be open to HTTP POST-requests and able to receive the payload containing the updated cargo. The payload structure can be found at the Webhook events section. ### Webhook authentication Each request (message) that we post to your webhook is accompanied by a header named 'x-portbase-webhook' which contains a JSON Web Token (JWT). You can use this token to verify whether the request originated from Portbase. *For security reasons we strongly suggest that you implement verification of this token in your webhook endpoint before handling the request*. In order to do so, our public RSA key for verification of the token signature can be found here. For more information on JSON Web Tokens you can see https://jwt.io/ For whitelisting you can use the following IP's: 34.253.113.23, 34.249.227.133, 34.253.114.17 # Testing For each API endpoint there is a so called stub available. These test endpoints accept valid requests and will respond with a valid dummy response in the correct schema format. The stubs can be used for testing and the validation of credentials, since they require a valid production environment authentication token. The URL of the stubs can be found at the specific endpoint in these API docs. ## Webhook testing ### Track requests In order to test your webhook implementation for tracking cargo you can add your webhook test url to the track-requests POST stub endpoint: Example JSON: ``` { "trackRequests": [ { "blNumber": "SCAC2345678901", "transportEquipmentNumber": "CONT9434134", "referenceNumber": "RF37290523", "labels": [] } ], "webhookUrl": "https://your.webhook.site" } ``` ### Inland operator nominations In order to test your webhook implementation for nominating inland operators you can add stub settings to the inland-operator-nominations PUT stub endpoint. You will receive a webhook update with the added inland operator nominations. Example JSON: ``` { "stubSettings": { "webhookUrl": "https://your.webhook.site", "blNumber": "SCAC2345678901", "referenceNumber": "RF37290523" }, ... Rest of your request } ``` ## Webhook test explained You will receive 5 updates per tracked trackRequest on your webhook. Any trackRequest(s) which are rejected or notTracked will not receive updates. The updates will be sent in intervals of 2 seconds each. * Update 1: Regular Bill of Lading * Update 2: ETA updated * Update 3: Inspection added * Update 4: ATA registered * Update 5: Discharge report added Understanding the impact of changed or new data, will have a significant increase in logistical value adapting our API. Therefore, please use the next section when implementing our API.

> Note that for using this endpoint additional authorisation for the Portbase Secure Chain is required. Please contact sales@portbase.com in order to obtain the authorisation.

This endpoint can be used to nominate an inland operator for transport equipment(s) listed on a Bill of Lading for which your organisation is Cargo Director.
After tracking a Bill of Lading, you will receive a track request id in the response which you will need to nominate an inland operator.
Besides nominating an inland operator it is also possible to send the transport order to the inland operator.

### Withdraw inland operator nominations
With this endpoint it is also possible to withdraw / delete an existing inland operator nomination for a transport equipment by leaving field `inlandOperator` empty / blank.
In that case, the entire shipment will be withdrawn / deleted.

put.description: > Note that for using this endpoint additional authorisation for the Portbase Secure Chain is required. Please contact sales@portbase.com in order to obtain the authorisation. This endpoint can be used to assign a cargo director for transport equipment(s) listed on a Bill of Lading for which your organisation is currently Cargo Director. After transfer you will no longer be the current Cargo director for the listed equipments. In the secure chain you will remain the former Cargo Director and, if applicable, the release-to party.

post.description: This endpoint can be used to track cargo. After tracking cargo, it's possible to receive real-time updates through our webhook functionality. Please refer to the Webhook events section for more information. > Please note that for testing purposes there is a stub endpoint available. The URL can be found in the dropdown above the 'Request samples' section to the right. This test endpoint bases its response on the **reference number** in your track request. The following prefixes of the value of **reference number** can be used to control the track response: > * NT: will appear under 'notTrackedBLs' in the response > * RE: will appear under 'rejectedBLs' in the response > * Any other value or no value: will appear under 'trackedBLs' in the response **Please note**: It is possible to add an optional **webhook url** for testing purposes. This url can be added on the same level as the "trackRequests" in the JSON and needs to be a valid url. Please refer to the 'samples' sections to the right for example objects of requests and responses. For more information about the content of requests and responses, see below.

get.description: Real-time updates on tracked cargo can be received through our webhook functionality (see Webhook events section). Additionally, this trackedBls endpoint can be used to retrieve information on tracked cargo in case your system missed webhook updates and is in need of synchronization. ***NOTE: This trackedBls endpoint is not meant for continuous synchronization and is throttled & monitored accordingly.*** > For testing purposes there is a stub endpoint available. The URL can be found in the dropdown above the 'Response samples' section to the right. The request parameter 'id' is required, however it will not be validated, so anything can be entered. The endpoint will always return the same dummy data enriched with the id in your request and adjusted to the current date and time. Please refer to the 'Response samples' to the right for an example object. For more information about the response schema, see the 'Responses' section below.

deepSeaEta.description: Estimated time of arrival of the deepsea vessel at the terminal. Format: yyyy-MM-ddThh:mm:ssZ

deepSeaTerminal.description: Code of the terminal. Possible values: SMDGn BICS code or Portbase short name. E.g.: MDT, NLMVII, DCD, EMX, RWG, RST. This value will be provided by the API updates.

deepSeaVesselName.description: Name of the deepsea vessel that is delivering the cargo

deepSeaVesselImo.description: IMO code of the deepsea vessel that is delivering the cargo

deepSeaVoyageNumber.description: Voyage number of the deepsea vessel that is delivering the cargo

equipmentNumber.description: Transport equipment number (for example a container number)

sizeType.description: Size type code (e.g. 4230) of the container

containerOperator.description: Carrier (i.e. shipping company) responsible for the deep sea transport of the cargo. Possible values: A 4-letter SCAC (Standard Carrier Alpha Code) or Portbase short name.

placeOfDestination.description: Final destination of the cargo, preferably UN code but name is also allowed

inlandTerminalLocation.description: Location UN code of the inland terminal

inlandTerminalCode.description: BICS code of the inland terminal. See https://binnenvaart.org/terminal-codes/ for all the barge terminals.

inlandOperator.description: Operator authorised to perform the inland transport of the cargo. Value: EAN code

inlandModality.description: The modality of the inland transport. Possible values: barge, rail or road

releaseReference.description: Reference number (i.e. pin code) from the carrier after the cargo’s commercial release

transportOrder.description: Details relating to the transport order given by the cargo director to the inland operator

invoiceReference.description: Reference to use when invoicing the inland transport

debtorName.description: Name of party that owes money for the inland transport

consigneeName.description: Name of the consignee that is importing the cargo

releaseExpiration.description: Expiration moment of the commercial release. Format: yyyy-MM-ddThh:mm:ssZ

demurrage.description: Number of free days at terminal. Number in whole days.

detention.description: Number of free days to deliver equipment to inland terminal. Number in whole days.

returnTerminal.description: The name of the terminal or depot where the empty equipment is returned. Preferably BICS or SMDG code but name is also allowed.

returnReference.description: The code that is required by terminal or depot to accept the equipment

destinationTargetDate.description: Date on which the equipment preferably should have reached the destination. Format: yyyy-MM-dd

destinationReference.description: The code that is required by the inland terminal to accept the empty equipment

destinationInstructions.description: Instructions on how to deliver the equipment at the destination

customsCategory.description: Three-letter customs category code for the inland transport. Possible values: IM4,MRN,DIN,FWV,ICT,NAR,NT1,BXI,TNK,PIE,PPZ.

documentNumber.description: The movement reference number (MRN) from customs of the inland movement

documentExpiration.description: Expiration date of MRN document. Format: yyyy-MM-dd

deepSeaEta.description: Estimated time of arrival of the deepsea vessel at the terminal. Format: yyyy-MM-ddThh:mm:ssZ

deepSeaTerminal.description: Code of the terminal. Possible values: SMDGn BICS code or Portbase short name. E.g.: MDT, NLMVII, DCD, EMX, RWG, RST. This value will be provided by the API updates.

deepSeaVesselName.description: Name of the deepsea vessel that is delivering the cargo

deepSeaVesselImo.description: IMO code of the deepsea vessel that is delivering the cargo

deepSeaVoyageNumber.description: Voyage number of the deepsea vessel that is delivering the cargo

CargoDirector.description:
Use either the CoC number (for Dutch organisations) or the iamConnectedId of the assigned organisation. When both are filled out, the iamConnectedId will be ignored.
You can use the CoC or Iam id of your own organisation when you want to 'reclaim' the role for your organisation.

chamberOfCommerceNumber.description: Chamber of Commerce number of the assigned organisation. Can be used for Dutch organisations.

iamConnectedId.description: IamConnectedId of the assigned organisation. Can be used for non-Dutch organisations

equipmentNumbers.description: A list of unique equipment number(s)

director.description: This field is deprecated. Use `cargoDirector.chamberOfCommerceNumber` instead.

webhookUrl.description: Webhook url where update is sent to

transportEquipmentNumber.description: Transport equipment number (for example a container number)

referenceNumber.description: A reference relevant to your organisation

labels.description: Categorize your cargo with self defined labels

callReferenceNumber.description: Add a call reference number to your track request to track the visit before the manifest is registered within Portbase.

vesselImoCode.description: Add the IMO code of the related vessel to track the visit before the manifest is registered within Portbase. If the CRN is filled out, the value of the IMO code will be ignored.

trackedBLs.description:
If the combination of blNumber and equipmentNumber is known in our system, the Track Request will appear in this list.
The B/L is successfully tracked and you will automatically receive the B/L data (and every future update) on your webhook url.

NB: if you are already successfully tracking this B/L (e.g. because someone already added it via the web interface),
the Track Request will still appear in this list. However, a reference number or labels in the (new) track request will be ignored.

notTrackedBLs.description:
If the combination of blNumber and equipmentNumber is not known in Cargo Controller (yet), the Track Request will appear in this list.
We will save the Track Request so ***you do not have to include this Track Request again in future requests to this endpoint***.
The saved Track Request will automatically be tracked when the B/L becomes known in our system. It will then be sent as an update to your webhook.

rejectedBLs.description:
If the handling agent has withdrawn your access to its cargo data, the Track Request will appear in this list together with the agent's name.
Please contact the handling agent for more information.

code.description: The error code sent by the terminal

parsedReason.description: A user friendly description of the error code

post.description: After tracking a Bill of Lading (see Track requests section), it is possible to receive updates on this Bill of Lading through your preconfigured webhook. > NOTE: it is best practice to offload all updates as quick as possible to a queue or messaging bus and process them asynchronously. This will prevent our system to wait not longer than necessary for responses. If, for some reason, a response is not received within that 10 second window, we assume the webhook has been received successfully. Response bodies will be discarded and never evaluated. We are aware that the impact of some updates in API have significant impact on the operational logistical flow. To make you aware of these events we have set out a few scenarios and what action must be taken after receiving such updates. | Event in Cargo Controller | Update in API | Logistical impact | |------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | Update of a Vessel Visit (ETA, ATA, ETD, ATD) | the (expected) arrivel time or any information in the `billOfLading.vesselVisit` changed | Planned resources (transport and warehouse) must be updated with new arrival data. | | Update of Manifest or Bill of Lading | any information in the manifest data of the `billOfLading` changed | The carrier has changed the value on which the import booking was based. B/L information is a basic value and could have a significant effect on any customs declarations. | | Deletion of Bill of Lading | `billOfLading.deleted` will be `true`. This will be set back to `false` when the Bill of Lading is registered again.| The carrier has removed this B/L from the manifest. In most cases this implies the cargo is not on board of this vessel. See this FAQ for more information. | | Discharge Terminal update | `dischargeTerminal` changes | The impact can be severe but is determined by the NID status. When the NID was already in place before the change, you must submit the NID again for the new terminal. See this FAQ for more information.| | Inspection notification/update of a Transport Equipment | an item will be added to the `inspectionItem` list with status `NOTIFIED` | Customs have determined that your cargo will be inspected and will not be available until customs gives a release. | | Release of an Inspection | `inspectionItem.status` will be `RELEASED` | When an inspection notification is lifted by customs, the pickup of said equipment can be planned (if all other mandatory actions have been carried out). | | Discharge Confirmation of a Transport Equipment | an item will be added to the `dischargeReports` list | A confirmation for each container/equipment on the B/L that is unloaded on the terminal. | | Import Document Notification sent to the Terminal | the document code will be added to the `transportEquipmentDeclarations` list (see example in 'Request samples') | A confirmation of the type of NID and the list of equipment’s that is involved. This list should be equal to the list of equipment’s registered on the B/L. Otherwise the missing equipment is not ready for pickup. | | Update of inland operator nominations | `nominatedInlandOperators` will be added add root level | For each equipment, an Inland Operator must be registered. If not, the pickup will not be possible as the Inland Operator will be verified for said container at the terminal gate. | | Update of Hinterland Pre Notifications by inland operators | an item will be added to the `hinterlandPreNotifications` list | For each equipment, we will confirm a valid preNotification for pickup by the inland operator on the terminal. If not, the pickup is not planned by the inland operator. | | Additional handling data from terminal | an item will be added to the `hinterlandTerminalData` list | This additional information is helpful to optimize the logistics planning. Some terminals require an additional subscription. > Please note that all timestamps are in ISO format with Zulu time, identified by a 'Z' at the end, e.g "2022-09-20T14:30:59Z". Zulu time is equal to UTC+0. For configuration details, please see Receive and process Webhook events section

200.description: OK - Please return this code if our call to your webhook was received and processed successfully.

5xx.description: Server error - Will trigger a retry (3 times).

default.description: All other response codes that we receive will not trigger a retry.
